text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Prime minister Tiit Vaehi dismissed accusations he illegally bought an appartment in Tallinn.

- Lithuanian parliament speaker Vytautas Landsbergis and Estonian speaker Toomas Savi signed a joint statement, stressing the importance of the Baltic states' security and their integration into Europe.
- Parliament added to the list of strategically important companies firms that will be formed on the basis of the power stations, oil shale producers and distillers.
- Parliament ratified a 176 million kroon loan from the World Bank, the money will be spent on promoting agriculture.
- Interviews with leading members of political parties on the allegedly illegal sales of flats in Tallinn to prominent politicians.
- Children in the northeastern Oru town where the main employer the Peat Industry went bankrupt are said to suffer from malnutrition. A trade union leader demands the government's assistance.

- Russian Metropolitan Cyril arrived yesterday in Tallinn at the invitation of Archbishop Cornelius, the head of Estonia's Moscow-led Orthodox congregations. No information was given on Cyril's agenda.
- The coastal town of Parnu opened a new sewage and water purification plant, built with 13.5 million kroon aid from Finland.
- Four Estonian dairy companies received a certificate for exporting milk products to Brazil.
- The mayor of Tallinn, Robert Lepikson, plans to cut the expenses of the city government by a third. Among the planned measures is limiting the use of service vehicles and mobile phones.
- German Volkswagen and company Eesti Talleks reached an agreement according to which the latter firm will become the exporter of Volkswagen cars to Estonia.
